# RQ-PHX-LAUNCHSTALLBANNER57: the Lanes pane says when the fleet stopped launching

## What Mason now sees
At the top of the desktop Lanes pane, when the fleet is reporting, a `role="status"` banner shows up only when something is stuck:
- "No job has launched for 42 min. 37 jobs are queued." (real numbers: the latest run of dispatchd.log ticks with work queued and `launched=0`, first tick to last; shown once it passes 30 min, the same limit as `phm fleet launch-stall`).
- One row per stuck lane, for example "codex-personal: 3 jobs waiting, oldest 61 min". Clicking a row calls `requestLaneFocus(lane)` and the pane scrolls to that lane. These are lanes whose status.json says running 0 while jobs older than 45 min wait (`readFleetLaneStall`).
- If the dispatcher log can't be read: "Phantom can't read the dispatcher log on this computer." The banner never shows a bare "unknown".
- Nothing is shown while loading, on error, when the route returns 404, or when nothing is stuck. Lane names and job ids are plain text. The banner uses existing CSS classes only, so no new colors. It refreshes every 30 s while visible.

## Deviation from the brief: how the route is mounted (verse-api.ts is untouched)
`/api/verse/fleet/control/*` belongs only to the `fleet-control` workbench family. `dispatchWorkbenchModules` sends every path under that prefix to the family and answers 404 itself. The one exception is the hard-coded `holds` path. So a new A10 entry in `verse-api.ts` would never be reached. Making it reachable would take three changes in that file: a new `MountedApiModuleId`, a new exemption in `dispatchWorkbenchModules`, and an update to the exhaustive `Record` in `test/verse-api-mount-310.test.ts`.

Instead, `fleet-control-api.ts` delegates that one exact path to the new module through a lazy `import()` (3 lines), the same way `stray-slots` is served. Non-GET requests first pass the family's dispatch and mutation-token gate, then the module answers 405.

## API
`GET /api/verse/fleet/control/launch-stall` returns `{ v: 1, generatedAt, stall: LaunchStallReport | null, lanes, source: 'ok' | 'unavailable' }`.
- It reads at most the last 512 KiB of `dispatchd.log` (`readLogTail`: one positioned read; the partial first line is dropped).
- If the log or the queue can't be read, `source` is `'unavailable'` and that part is `stall: null` or `lanes: []`. It never invents zeros and never returns a 500.
- `startTime`, lane names and job ids pass through `scrubSecrets`.
- The runs directory is `ASHLR_RUNS_DIR` or `~/.ashlr-runs`, the same as the CLI.

## Files (10; the brief expected about 9)
- `src/core/fleet/launch-stall-read.ts` (new): pure `parseLaunchStall` and the `LaunchStallReport` type, moved out of the CLI unchanged.
- `src/cli/fleet-launch-stall.ts`: now calls `parseLaunchStall`. Output and exit codes are unchanged; its 8 existing tests pass untouched. The CLI-local interface was removed because nothing else imported it.
- `src/core/verse/fleet-launch-stall-api.ts` (new): the handler, `readLaunchStallView` and `readLogTail`.
- `src/core/verse/fleet-control-api.ts`: the 3-line delegation (explained above), in place of the single `verse-api.ts` line.
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-lanes/launch-stall-queries.ts` (new): validator, 404 → null.
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-lanes/LaunchStallBanner.tsx` (new).
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-lanes/FleetLanesPane.tsx`: 2 lines to mount the banner.
- Tests (new): `test/launch-stall-read.test.ts`, `test/verse-fleet-launch-stall-api.test.ts`, `src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-lanes/LaunchStallBanner.test.tsx`.

The tenth file is the one-file swap above: `fleet-control-api.ts` replaces the expected `verse-api.ts` edit. The `fleet-holds-api.ts` GET has no extra gate, so this GET has none either.

title: Publish a green ancestor release-please tag
body: ## What & why The release train can publish a release-please tag that is an ancestor of master when required CI on that exact SHA is green. Security review of `6431a59d` plus the downstream publish path are both in this update. - Release-build and attest no longer use `startsWith('refs/tags/v')`. A shell step matches `^refs/tags/v(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)$` against `RELEASE_REF`, or `refs/heads/master`. `releaseHeadBranch` rejects `refs/heads/vX.Y.Z`. - Build, attest, publish, and the cadence tag lookup re-peel annotated and lightweight tags. Attest `prepare` requires `GITHUB_SHA == CANDIDATE_SHA`. - Required check-runs are paginated. A page whose `total_count` does not match the rows returned is `unknown` and is not published. - `verifyAttestation --source-ref` accepts only `refs/heads/master` or `refs/tags/vX.Y.Z` whose peeled sha is `candidate_sha`. The npm attestor check uses the same rule. Compare stays `candidate...master` status `ahead` or `identical`, with green required CI. - `contrib/mac/release-autorun.sh`, its tests, and the README hunks match master. Security is pinning the live Mac copy separately. - Compare direction, permissions, env refs, `assertReleaseWrite`, the dirty-tree check, the secret-shape scan, signing, notarization, retagging, and tag deletion are unchanged. ## How it was verified - `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` (eslint, `tsgo --noEmit`, authority drift) - `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/release-train.test.ts test/canonical-npm-publisher.test.ts test/m30.ci.test.ts` (130 tests) - `python3 -I contrib/mac/tests/test_release_autorun.py` (35 tests, the master suite) - `node --test` on the attestation-input, release-fast-smoke, and release-cadence suites - `bash -n contrib/mac/release-autorun.sh` ## Out-of-repo follow-ups This PR does not write under `~/.ashlr-runs` and no longer proposes a change to the in-repo Mac observer. Security is pinning `~/.ashlr-runs/bin/release-autorun.sh` separately. `~/.ashlr-runs/bin/release-sign.sh` is not in this repo. Draft only. Not marked ready, not enqueued, not merged. Security will mark it ready.

body:

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-YIELDTRIAGEN9Q8

Task: inspect queue generation and dispatch code and their tests; prevent
repeated empty jobs using recent outcomes and concrete repository evidence;
tests for duplicate candidates, stale evidence, and recovery when files change.

## Summary

Target: `src/core/drive/queuegen.ts` — the fleet-PR queue generator that
writes `- READY` FIXUP/REBASE lines (host: `scripts/queuegen.mjs`). Its
dedupe was a single `{id, at}` clock record per `repo#pr`: an unchanged head
suppressed forever inside 24 h even after a push, and nothing consulted
`jobs.jsonl`, so a candidate that repeatedly ran empty kept coming back.

- New `src/core/queue/job-outcomes.ts`: parses `jobs.jsonl` lines and
  collapses latest-per-job into `{at, empty, merged}` (newest row wins per
  spec section "records use job, event, ts…") — empty counts only when
  `empty: true` and no merged outcome.
- `queuegen.ts`: `QueuegenEmission` now records `{id, at, headSha, check,
  file}` and state keeps a bounded (≤8/PR) history, newest first, while
  `normalizeState` still accepts legacy single-record state.
  - Dedupe: same head inside the window dedupes before any `gh` call;
    `headSha === undefined` legacy records keep clock-only behavior.
    A moved head releases the dedupe (new candidate, new deterministic id).
  - Suppression: after evidence is gathered (failing check/`merge-tree` +
    resolved file), `countEmptyStreak` counts the newest contiguous
    same-signature attempts with a fresh (`at <= now`, inside window)
    `empty: true`/`merged !== true` outcome. Streak ≥ 2 suppresses
    (`QUEUEGEN_EMPTY_STREAK`, `summary.suppressed++`).
  - A changed check or file is a different candidate — recovery when files
    change. A productive or merged outcome breaks the streak. Missing,
    stale or unreadable outcome evidence never suppresses; a throwing
    `recentJobOutcomes` reader logs `QUEUEGEN_OUTCOMES_UNAVAILABLE` once
    and the cycle continues unsuppressed (advisory, fails open).
- `scripts/queuegen.mjs`: `--metrics <file>` flag (default
  `~/.ashlr-runs/metrics/jobs.jsonl`) feeding `recentJobOutcomes()` — a
  tail-bounded (last 32 KB / 200 rows) read of the jobs ledger; the core
  stays filesystem-free.
- `docs/QUEUE.md`: new "Queuegen dedupe and empty-outcome suppression"
  section documenting the evidence and fail-open semantics.

Dispatch side inspected: `contrib/mac/restock.py` already tracks
empty-streaks for `single_case_group` jobs and `dedupeQueue`
(`src/core/queue/dedupe.ts`) marks repeated acceptance+file READY lines
SUPERSEDED — generation-side suppression upstream of both keeps this
change self-contained; no dispatch behavior changed.

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/queuegen.test.ts test/job-outcomes.test.ts`
  — 2 files, 41 tests, all pass.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/queuegen.test.ts test/job-outcomes.test.ts
  test/queue-dedupe.test.ts test/dispatch*.test.ts` (broader queuegen set)
  — 4 files, 64 tests, all pass.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/doc-facts.test.ts` — 1 file,
  6 tests, all pass.
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — pass: file selection, authority
  drift, `tsc --noEmit`, realio lane lint, verse sync-I/O lint, dedupe.
- `node_modules/.bin/eslint src/core/drive/queuegen.ts
  src/core/queue/job-outcomes.ts test/queuegen.test.ts
  test/job-outcomes.test.ts scripts/queuegen.mjs` — clean.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run check:docs` — 0 errors.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

## Net LOC

+577 / −33 across 6 files (`src/core/drive/queuegen.ts`, `scripts/queuegen.mjs`,
`docs/QUEUE.md`, `test/queuegen.test.ts`, new `src/core/queue/job-outcomes.ts`,
new `test/job-outcomes.test.ts`) → net +544.

## Notes / limitations

- First-failing-required-check ordering decides the FIXUP signature; if a PR
  alternates between two failing checks the streak resets (conservative —
  emits, never over-suppresses).
- Suppression needs the job id in `jobs.jsonl` (`job`/`job_id`/`jobId`),
  matching dispatchd's ledger rows.
- No commit/push; changes are uncommitted in this worktree.

- `phm fleet merge-latency` (`src/cli/fleet-merge-latency.ts`): reads the
  `~/.ashlr-runs/metrics/merge-events.jsonl` ledger; per-PR stage timings

  `wait_by_reason_s`), pending auto-merges, and the `queue_retries`

title: Attest owner spend budgets above zero
body: ## What & why Follow-up to #4229. Do not revert that change. The owner USD budget still defaults to 0, but the only write check was `AGENT_ENV_MARKERS`, and the budget file is mode 0600 on the same account. An agent could unset the markers and run `phm budget set`, or write the file directly, and grant itself spend. A stored amount above 0 now counts only when the file carries an attestation the reader can verify: - **pin-chain:** the policy hash is the detail of a verified authority-ledger note written as actor `mason`, and the attestation names that note's chain hash - **mason-approval:** an applied operator approval of kind `spend-budget` records that same digest as its action id A missing, malformed, or mismatched attestation, or a parse error, fails closed to an effective budget of 0. The budget path is `realHome()/.ashlr/spend-budget.json`, so `HOME` and `ASHLR_HOME` cannot point the reader at a decoy. The ledger and the approval file are trusted only when the process home is that account home. `phm budget set` still refuses agent markers, and it also refuses unless stdin and stdout are a TTY. ## How it was verified - [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean - [x] `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` (eslint on changed files, tsgo, authority drift) - [ ] `npm run build` not run - [x] `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/spend-budget.test.ts` — 8 passed - [x] `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run dev -- verify-safety` — 5/5 ## Safety checklist - [x] No new outward capability - [x] Budget guard strengthened: nonzero spend requires an owner attestation, and non-TTY `budget set` is refused - [x] No new runtime dependencies - [x] No secrets logged ## Notes Same-account code can still append a ledger note or an operator approval and then write a matching budget file. The CLI path cannot: it needs a real terminal, and a hand-written file with no matching attestation stays at 0.
